title: Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs — Tracking, Borrower Notices and Placement of Certificates
content:
**Tracking.** On every tier of the **Lender-Placed Flood Master Programs** Tidemark tracks the lender's loans and mails borrower notices on the lender's behalf.

**Notices.** When the Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form (FEMA Form 086-0-32) shows the building in a Special Flood Hazard Area and the borrower's flood coverage has lapsed or is below the mandatory purchase amount, a first notice is mailed to the borrower stating the required amount; a reminder (second) notice is mailed 15 calendar days before the earliest placement date.

**Conditions for issuing a certificate.**

1. A certificate is issued only after more than 45 calendar days (the borrower notice period) have passed since the first notice is mailed, counted by adding the days to the notice date on the calendar, the last day of the notice period not qualifying. The mailing date of the first notice on the loan's tracking record is the starting point.
2. A certificate is issued only under a program whose status is active.
3. No certificate is placed on a building outside a Special Flood Hazard Area.
4. No certificate is issued when acceptable borrower evidence was received before placement. **This sentence is no longer in force for a placement priced under the residential placement schedule or the commercial placement schedule, each of which follows its own reading of borrower evidence; for every other placement it continues to apply.**
5. No more than 1 certificate may be in force on one loan.

| Day, counted on the calendar from the first-notice mailing date | Notice condition |
|---|---|
| Any day up to and including the 45th day after the notice date | Not met |
| The 46th day after the notice date or later | Met |

*Boundary illustration (hypothetical):* the day reached by adding 45 days to a hypothetical notice date is the last day of the notice period and does not qualify; the next day does.

**Determination disputes.** A borrower and lender who dispute the determination may jointly ask FEMA for a Letter of Determination Review within 45 calendar days of the borrower's notification; the request does not stop placement, and a FEMA decision removing the building from the area is handled under the loan-event cancellation rule.

## Points of judgement

- *The program is suspended.* Condition 2 is not met: no certificate is issued until the program is active again.
- *A review request is pending with FEMA.* The request alone does not stop placement.

superseded_clauses: No certificate is issued when acceptable borrower evidence was received before placement
